title: Dispatch: S44 repair - SRD 0-HP summon lifecycle and remove-policy integrity (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Repair for PR #599 review finding S44 (review 5403780189 at head 7414d014; S43 withdrawn in 5403787349), widened by the user on 2026-10-03 to every SRD contradiction in the same defect class.

GOVERNING RULE (user, hard blocker; bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): no change may modify or contradict the SRD in letter or spirit. Before each behaviour decision, read the governing record text in packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json (data.description plus data.mechanics.effects[*].transitions).

SOURCE AUTHORITY
- Conjure Animals, Conjure Celestial, Conjure Elemental, Conjure Fey, Conjure Minor Elementals, Conjure Woodland Beings: "disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or when the spell ends". Records carry transition {trigger:'zero-hit-points', changes:[effect->ended, presence->absent]}.
- Find Familiar / Find Steed: "When the [familiar|steed] drops to 0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form" (transition zero-hp-absence, presence->absent). Both spells are instantaneous, so start_effect refuses them as spell sources (activeEffects.ts ~2600); they can only be modelled as ruling-sourced summoning effects.
- Simulacrum: "lasts until it drops to 0 hit points, at which point it reverts to snow and melts instantly" (zero-hp-destruction, integrity->destroyed).
- Animate Objects / Giant Insect: 0 HP -> form->original (reversion; Animate Objects also carries remaining damage over to the object). This family is NOT a disappearance and is OUT OF SCOPE for 0-HP behaviour (follow-up bead). It is in scope for the guards in (C).
- rule:monsters-and-death: the GM may give mighty villains and special NPCs player-character death rules. A summon whose spell overrides 0 HP can never be dying, stable, knocked out, or a corpse.
- S1 design (docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/2026-07-06-o9bd-18-7-9-s1-summoning-contract-design.md lines 129-142) assigns 0-HP removal to F3 runtime as engine-pending. The engine has never executed it: summoningSchema.ts is consumed only by validation.

DEFECTS BEING REPAIRED
1. S44: activeEffects.ts removeProjection (~2401-2412, added in 7414d014 for S42) returns 'released' for a dead/dying/stable summon under a stored 'remove' policy. That silently turns F3 remove into release and erases the end-vs-break distinction.
2. Root SRD gap: an effect-owned summon at 0 HP becomes 'dead' (monster rules), 'dying'/'stable' (player-character rules), or 'unconscious' (knockout) and stays in play. The source says it disappears.
3. update_combatant deathRules:'player-character' (and the knockout statuses) can be applied to such a summon, contradicting its spell.
4. A dead summon cannot leave play when its spell ends, because I8 (dead is terminal) refuses 'inactive'. On main this worked; I8 is new in this PR.
5. Sibling: a campaign_actor-target actor link with remove calls updateCampaignActor(status:'inactive'). With no active projection, that overwrites a dying actor's status (life state lost); with an active projection it throws, which is reported as 'missing'.
6. Sibling: caller-declared cleanup policies can contradict the spell (e.g. Conjure Animals with cleanupOnEnd 'release' keeps the beasts after the spell ends).

DESIGN (supervisor decisions; do not re-decide; stop and report in bd notes if one is impossible)

A. New status 'absent' = out of play under a rule (vanished, melted, removed by its owning effect). Add it to CombatantStatus, ActorStatus, CombatantLifeStatus, and to the status CHECK of encounter_combatant and campaign_actor through migration 0039 (table rebuild, same pattern as 0033_combatant_death_rules.sql; keep every other column/constraint/index byte-identical). Update any migration list or schema registry and its tests.
   - Engine-owned: update_combatant / update_campaign_actor refuse an explicit 'absent' (as 'dying' is refused today).
   - A combatant that is absent is not a participant: no turn, no action economy, no death saves, no stabilize, no stable recovery, no suffocation, no healing or damage, no condition writes. Refuse those writes with a clear error, using the same mechanism that refuses writes to dead combatants.
   - Lifecycle invariants: absent requires stableRecovery null, recoveryBlock null, and death-save counters 0. I8 is amended so that dead may become absent and nothing else. Absent never returns to any other status on the same combatant row.
   - Projection to the campaign actor maps absent->absent. The S41 rule (monster 0 HP with no terminal cause projects as unconscious) must not turn absent into unconscious.
   - Admitting an absent campaign actor to an encounter is a new manifestation. It is allowed only when the admission supplies hp > 0; it then starts alive with a fresh lifecycle (death saves 0, no schedule). Without supplied hp, refuse with a message naming the absence. The actor's status becomes alive.

B. Zero-HP rule as a durable creature property. Add a nullable column zero_hp_rule TEXT CHECK (zero_hp_rule IN ('vanish','revert')) on encounter_combatant (in 0039), mirrored into campaign actor state through the existing actor/projection sync so it survives admission and combat close.
   - Set at start_effect for each owned actor. For a spell-sourced summoning effect, derive it from the record: any mechanics.effects[*].transitions entry with trigger 'zero-hit-points' whose changes include presence->absent or integrity->destroyed => 'vanish'; one whose changes include form->original => 'revert'. For any source kind, the actor input may declare atZeroHitPoints: 'vanish' (new optional field on EffectActorLinkInput and the start_effect actors schema), so a ruling-sourced Find Familiar/Find Steed can be modelled truthfully. A declaration that contradicts a derived value is refused.
   - Releasing a link does not clear the property: a Conjure Elemental/Fey released by a concentration break is still subject to zero-hp-removal (its transition admits control 'uncontrolled').
   - Implement 'vanish' in the PURE lifecycle (combatantLifecycle.ts): add zeroHpRule to CombatantLifecycleState. Every event that brings HP from >0 to 0 (damage, knockout, suffocationDrop, exhaustionChanged clamping effective max to 0, headDied, any other) yields status 'absent' instead of dead/dying/stable/unconscious. The exception is exhaustion level 6, which is death, not 0 HP. Keep the existing behaviour for that case and confirm it against the exhaustion record.
   - A knockout request (status 'unconscious' or 'stable' with damage to 0) on a 'vanish' or 'revert' creature is refused, citing the spell.
   - In the persistence adapter, after persisting a transition into absent caused by 0 HP, in the same transaction:
     (i) break the creature's own concentration, if any, with cause owner-removed;
     (ii) close its active actor link, if any, with status 'removed' and removed_reason 'zero-hit-points';
     (iii) if that effect now has no active actor links, end it through the normal F3 end path with reason 'source-removed' (cleanup mode 'end').
   - Report the vanish in the update result (e.g. vanished: { effectId|null, rule:'vanish' }) and in the model-facing tool result text.
   - Out-of-combat path: updateCampaignActor reducing hpCurrent to 0 for an actor whose zero_hp_rule is 'vanish' and that has no active projection applies the same outcome (actor status absent, link closed, effect possibly ended).
   - 'revert' gets no automatic 0-HP behaviour in this change (follow-up). It is used only by the guards in C.

C. Guards (make the S44 state unrepresentable):
   - update_combatant deathRules:'player-character' is refused when the combatant's zero_hp_rule is non-null, or when the combatant (or its campaign actor) is the projection of an ACTIVE actor link whose cleanup_on_end or cleanup_on_break is 'remove'. The message names the reason: the spell's 0-HP rule, or that a remove-policy owner must be able to take it out of play.
   - start_effect refuses an actor link over a combatant that already uses player-character death rules when the derived zero_hp_rule is non-null or either policy is 'remove'.
   - Result: under 'remove', a dying or stable creature is unreachable.

D. F3 remove for actor links: add an internal engine seam, removeCombatantFromPlay / removeCampaignActorFromPlay, that sets status 'absent' (and on the actor and its active projection for a campaign_actor target).
   - Status alive, unconscious, escaped, inactive, or dead => absent, reported 'removed'. Already absent => 'removed' (idempotent).
   - Status dying or stable => throw an internal invariant error (unreachable by C; never translate the action).
   - A holder that is truly unreachable (deleted, closed instance) stays 'missing'.
   - REVERT the S42 'released' branch. removeProjection's return type goes back to 'removed' | 'missing'. 'released' only ever comes from a stored 'release' policy.
   - Defect 5 is fixed by routing the campaign_actor path through the seam.

E. Cleanup policies for spell-sourced summoning effects with a summoning profile (presence family only):
   - If the record has a 'spell-ended' transition changing presence->absent, cleanupOnEnd must be 'remove'.
   - If it has a 'concentration-broken' transition that does not change presence (Conjure Elemental/Fey: control->uncontrolled), cleanupOnBreak must be 'release'.
   - Otherwise, if the spell requires concentration and the spell-ended transition removes presence, cleanupOnBreak must be 'remove'.
   - An omitted policy takes the derived value; an explicit contradiction is refused with the record text.
   - Form, duplicate, and persistent-linked families: no new constraint.

F. Model-facing text and docs must be truthful and match the code. Update:
   - update_combatant description and its deathRules property;
   - start_effect actors description and new atZeroHitPoints;
   - the end_effect / cleanup action description, if it mentions inactive or released;
   - docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md: §8 cleanup (remove => absent; dying/stable unreachable), §9 S1 summons (0-HP rule executed for vanish; revert pending), defaults derived from the record.
   Grep for every 'inactive' produced by F3 remove (tests, docs, descriptions) and update each with the reason.

EVIDENCE (permanent; drive through the tool registry like packages/core/test/combatantRepairsBatchG.test.ts)
1. Actor-link policy matrix, replacing the S42 'missing'/'released' reproducer (delete or rewrite that test; do not keep it asserting 'released'):
   - alive x remove -> absent, 'removed';
   - alive x release -> still alive participant, 'released';
   - dead x remove -> absent, 'removed';
   - dying/stable x release (ruling summon, PC rules, release/release) -> unchanged participant, 'released';
   - dying x remove -> unreachable: assert both refusals (PC opt-in under remove policy; remove link over a PC combatant);
   - one effect with cleanupOnEnd 'remove' + cleanupOnBreak 'release': concentration break => 'released' + present; normal end => 'removed' + absent.
2. Zero-HP vanish:
   - Conjure Animals with two beasts: one takes damage to 0 => absent, never dead; link removed with reason zero-hit-points; effect still active. Second to 0 => effect ended with reason source-removed.
   - Conjure Elemental released by a concentration break, then damage to 0 => absent.
   - Suffocation drop and exhaustion-max-to-0 paths also vanish (one parameterised case).
   - Out-of-combat actor hp to 0 => absent.
3. Guards: PC opt-in refused on a Conjure Animals summon; knockout refused; contradicting cleanup policy refused; omitted policies derive (Conjure Elemental break => release).
4. Absent: re-admission without hp refused; with hp admitted alive; damage/heal/death-save on absent refused.
5. Migration 0039 upgrade test in the same style as the existing 0033/0036 migration tests, if those exist.
Each new test must fail on 7414d014 (negative proof: state it in the completion notes).

FOLLOW-UP to file with bd create (do not implement): Animate Objects / Giant Insect 0-HP form reversion (Animate Objects carry-over damage; Giant Insect normal-form state), and the Conjure Elemental/Fey cast-anchored absolute-time removal (+1 h).

VERIFY: npm run verify:worktree before committing (it rewrites files). It must be fully green.
acceptance_criteria: Every item in DESIGN A-F implemented; EVIDENCE 1-5 present through the tool registry and each fails on 7414d014 (negative proof recorded in notes); S42 'released' shortcut reverted; follow-up bead filed; npm run verify:worktree fully green before commit; completion report in bd notes; work committed on branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.17, not pushed.
notes:
COMPLETION (commit cf53c7c1, verify:worktree green: 323 files/5854 tests pass).
DESIGN: A absent status added to CombatantStatus/ActorStatus/CombatantLifeStatus + migration 0039 (rebuild of encounter_combatant incl. zero_hp_rule, campaign_actor status CHECK; data/schema.snapshot.sql regenerated; migration lists updated); explicit absent refused by update_combatant/updateCampaignActor; absent refuses damage/heal/conditions/status/deathSave/stabilize/suffocation/turns/usage counters/new effect participation; lifecycle invariants (absent: no schedule/block/counters; dead->absent only via removeFromPlay event; absent terminal; I1/I2/I4 tolerate absent); projection maps absent->absent; re-admission needs hpCurrent>0, starts alive fresh. B zero_hp_rule column + actor state.combatLifecycle.zeroHpRule; derived from record transitions at start_effect, atZeroHitPoints 'vanish' input/schema, contradictions refused; vanish in pure lifecycle for damage/clamp/exhaustion/suffocation, knockout refused; adapter breaks concentration (owner-removed), closes link (removed, zero-hit-points), ends effect source-removed when last owned creature; result reports vanished (+message in update_combatant); out-of-combat updateCampaignActor path. 'revert' only feeds guards (eshyra-ysr3). C guards in update_combatant and start_effect. D removeCombatantFromPlay/removeCampaignActorFromPlay seams; S42 released branch reverted (removeProjection returns removed|missing); dying/stable throws CombatantLifecycleInvariantError. E record-derived cleanup policies (spell-ended->remove, conc-broken w/o presence change->release, else conc->remove), explicit contradictions refused; tool now passes explicit 'remove'. F descriptions (update_combatant, start_effect, end_effect, begin_turn, set_suffocation) and docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md updated; existing tests asserting 'inactive' now assert 'absent'; three existing tests that linked PC-rules creatures under default remove now use release/release (encounterCombatants, exhaustion).
Note: headDied/zero-heads remain dead (terminal cause), not absent; exhaustion level 6 stays dead.
EVIDENCE: packages/core/test/zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts (policy matrix replacing the deleted S42 test in combatantRepairsBatchG.test.ts; vanish; guards; absent/re-admission); packages/core/test/migrationRunner.test.ts (migration 0039 upgrade). Negative proof: git archive of 7414d014 + these two test files: 14 of 16+ new tests fail (all but alive-x-release and dying/stable-x-release, which assert pre-existing release behaviour and pass on both).
Follow-ups: eshyra-ysr3 (Animate Objects/Giant Insect reversion, pre-filed by coordinator); Conjure Elemental/Fey +1h removal: eshyra-7vh3.
Supervisor review (Opus 5.5 captain): design A-F verified against spec + SRD record text. One defect fixed inline in 06cbb44f: re-admitting an absent actor carried over conditions/exhaustion/death rules/0-HP rule (new manifestation must be a new creature); test rewritten, negative-proved against cf53c7c1. verify:worktree green (5854 pass, 3 skip).
